title: 1962 AHSME Problem 9
statement: When \(x^9-x\) is factored as completely as possible into polynomials and monomials with integral coefficients, the number of factors is:

solutions.text:
Factoring over the integers gives \[ \begin{aligned} x^9-x &=x(x-1)(x+1)\\ &\quad\cdot(x^2+1)(x^4+1). \end{aligned} \] The last two nonconstant factors are irreducible over the integers, so there are \(5\) factors.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Begin with \(x(x^8-1)\) and repeatedly use differences of squares
Over the integers, stop after isolating \(x,\) \(x-1,\) \(x+1,\) \(x^2+1,\) and \(x^4+1\)
